title: The sheaf condition on a basis may be checked on a cofinal system of coverings
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology and satisfies $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal B$. A *$\mathcal B$-covering* of $U\in\mathcal B$ is a family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of members of $\mathcal B$ (any index set $I$, possibly empty) with $\bigcup_iU_i=U$; a $\mathcal B$-covering $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $U$ *refines* $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ if there is a map $\alpha:J\to I$ with $V_j\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}$ for all $j$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal B$: sets $\mathcal F(U)$ for $U\in\mathcal B$ and maps $s\mapsto s|_V:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$, with $s|_U=s$ and $(s|_V)|_W=s|_W$. Say that $\mathcal F$ satisfies the *gluing condition* for a $\mathcal B$-covering $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of $U$ if for every family $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ for all $i,j\in I$ there is exactly one $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $s|_{U_i}=s_i$ for all $i$. Suppose that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ a set $C(U)$ of $\mathcal B$-coverings of $U$ is given which is *cofinal*: every $\mathcal B$-covering of $U$ is refined by some member of $C(U)$. If $\mathcal F$ satisfies the gluing condition for every member of $C(U)$, for every $U\in\mathcal B$, then $\mathcal F$ satisfies the gluing condition for every $\mathcal B$-covering of every $U\in\mathcal B$. (Example: if every $\mathcal B$-covering of every $U\in\mathcal B$ is refined by a finite one, $C(U)$ may be the set of finite $\mathcal B$-coverings of $U$, including the empty covering of $U=\emptyset$.)

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Section 009H: Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case), whose proof is that of Lemma 009K (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings) with the coverings U_ij of U_i cap U_j the single member U_i cap U_j; Definition 009J (label definition-sheaf-basis) for the sheaf condition (**)

proof.text: *Notation and refinement.* Fix $U\in\mathcal B$ and an arbitrary $\mathcal B$-covering $\mathcal U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of $U$. By cofinality of $C(U)$ choose $\mathcal V=(V_j)_{j\in J}$ in $C(U)$ and a map $\alpha:J\to I$ with $V_j\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}$ for all $j$. All intersections below of members of $\mathcal B$ lie in $\mathcal B$ by hypothesis, so all restrictions written are defined.

source.place: Section 009H, proof of Lemma 009K, first paragraph

proof.text: *Uniqueness for an arbitrary $\mathcal B$-covering.* Let $s,s'\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $s|_{U_i}=s'|_{U_i}$ for all $i\in I$. For every $j\in J$, $s|_{V_j}=(s|_{U_{\alpha(j)}})|_{V_j}=(s'|_{U_{\alpha(j)}})|_{V_j}=s'|_{V_j}$ (transitivity of restriction). The family $(s|_{V_j})_j$ is compatible (both $(s|_{V_j})|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}$ and $(s|_{V_{j'}})|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}$ equal $s|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}$), and $s$ and $s'$ both glue it; by the uniqueness in the gluing condition for $\mathcal V\in C(U)$, $s=s'$. Since $U$ and $\mathcal U$ were arbitrary: (U) for every $W\in\mathcal B$ and every $\mathcal B$-covering $(W_k)_k$ of $W$, two sections of $\mathcal F(W)$ with the same restrictions to all $W_k$ are equal. (For the empty covering $I=\emptyset$ of $U=\emptyset$, the map $\alpha:J\to\emptyset$ forces $J=\emptyset$, so the empty covering of $\emptyset$ is in $C(\emptyset)$ and its gluing condition says that $\mathcal F(\emptyset)$ has exactly one element; the argument above covers this case, the hypotheses on $s,s'$ and on the family being vacuous.)

source.place: Section 009H, proof of Lemma 009K, second paragraph

proof.text: *A compatible family on $\mathcal V$.* Let $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\cap U_{i'}}=s_{i'}|_{U_i\cap U_{i'}}$ for all $i,i'\in I$. Put $t_j=s_{\alpha(j)}|_{V_j}\in\mathcal F(V_j)$. For $j,j'\in J$, $V_j\cap V_{j'}\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}\cap U_{\alpha(j')}$, hence $t_j|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}=s_{\alpha(j)}|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}=(s_{\alpha(j)}|_{U_{\alpha(j)}\cap U_{\alpha(j')}})|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}=(s_{\alpha(j')}|_{U_{\alpha(j)}\cap U_{\alpha(j')}})|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}=t_{j'}|_{V_j\cap V_{j'}}$. (In 009K this is the 'small kink', which needs the uniqueness of step 2 because there the overlaps are covered by arbitrary $U_{ii'k}$; with the single members $U_i\cap U_{i'}$ of the present gluing condition it is the displayed transitivity of restriction.) By the existence in the gluing condition for $\mathcal V\in C(U)$ there is $t\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $t|_{V_j}=t_j$ for all $j$.

source.place: Section 009H, proof of Lemma 009K, third and fourth paragraphs, with U_ijk = U_i cap U_j as in Lemma 009L

proof.text: *$t$ restricts to $s_i$.* Fix $i\in I$. The sets $W_j=U_i\cap V_j\in\mathcal B$, $j\in J$, form a $\mathcal B$-covering of $U_i$, since $\bigcup_jW_j=U_i\cap\bigcup_jV_j=U_i\cap U=U_i$. For each $j$, $W_j\subseteq U_i\cap U_{\alpha(j)}$, so $(t|_{U_i})|_{W_j}=t|_{W_j}=(t|_{V_j})|_{W_j}=t_j|_{W_j}=s_{\alpha(j)}|_{W_j}=(s_{\alpha(j)}|_{U_{\alpha(j)}\cap U_i})|_{W_j}=(s_i|_{U_i\cap U_{\alpha(j)}})|_{W_j}=s_i|_{W_j}$. So $t|_{U_i}$ and $s_i$ in $\mathcal F(U_i)$ have the same restriction to every member of the $\mathcal B$-covering $(W_j)_j$ of $U_i\in\mathcal B$; by (U) of step 2 applied to $W=U_i$, $t|_{U_i}=s_i$. (This is where the hypothesis on $C(U_i)$, not only on $C(U)$, is used.)

source.place: Section 009H, proof of Lemma 009K, last paragraph (the sets U_{i alpha(j) k} cap V_j, here U_i cap V_j, cover U_i; 'we leave it to the reader' written out)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 4 the section $t$ restricts to $s_i$ on every $U_i$, and by step 2 (for the covering $\mathcal U$ of $U$) it is the only section of $\mathcal F(U)$ doing so. Hence $\mathcal F$ satisfies the gluing condition for $\mathcal U$; as $U\in\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal U$ were arbitrary, for every $\mathcal B$-covering of every member of $\mathcal B$.
